I've been playing DnD for awhile.  I believe that the moves that Wizard's of the Coast are making is more about expanding on lore and re-imaging the alignment chart than it is about trying to be woke.  As the lore is being updated and fleshed out they are re-imagining cultures within the DnD Lore (They use Drow and Orcs as examples) that were originally only imagined as being evil creatures.  But it goes beyond just lore down to an original vestige of the mechanics of the game... the alignment chart.

With years of DnD behind us, any DM or player can ask themselves, what is the use of the alignment chart really?  Like it's there, but no one really uses much.  Once or twice during character creation but for the most part it's an abandoned mechanic the moment the adventure begins.  No one likes their character being stuck to an alignment track.  They just play their character as they think their character would be, which is often times just an extension of themselves.  They aren't trying to play their character to what the chart says.  They play their character and see where they fall on the chart.

The most notable DnD Character around, Drizzt, is a good aligned Drow that defies the original stereotype of Drow being only evil creatures.  Players have been making Good aligned orcs for years.  Critical Role is playing with a good aligned goblin.  Drow, Orcs, and Goblins are all typically evil creatures.  But the rules have no problem with them being played as non-evil characters.  So I see this as WotC just signaling that they are now going to start making the races more complex with culture that isn't stuck on the alignment chart track, something we (and WotC) do for players already.
